review_candidates.title: Software Engineer
review_candidates.description: About The Company The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) serves as the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and functions as a key IT competence hub for the Max Planck Society. With over four decades of experience, GWDG specializes in providing high-performance computing resources, supporting a diverse range of scientific disciplines including digital humanities, life sciences, earth system sciences, and engineering. The organization is recognized as one of the eight national high-performance computing centers within the German NHR network since 2020. GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is a strategic partner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Additionally, it manages HPC infrastructure for the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and actively participates in national and international research initiatives. In the realm of quantum computing, GWDG runs the QUICS project, offering SMEs access to quantum resources, highlighting its commitment to advancing cutting-edge research and technological innovation. About The Role We are seeking a highly motivated Quantum Software Engineer (m/f/d) to join our interdisciplinary HPC team within the "Computing" working group at GWDG. This full-time position (39 hours per week) is funded until October 2029 as part of the GWDG QC project. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in developing and expanding GWDG’s quantum computing ecosystem, with a focus on anomaly detection for industry applications. You will contribute to building a platform that leverages quantum computing technologies to provide companies with advanced tools for quantum anomaly detection. The role requires a strong background in software architecture, containerization, and security, along with the ability to verify code manually for security concerns, especially when handling sensitive data. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of quantum computing, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and applied computer science, within a stimulating academic and research environment. Qualifications The ideal candidate holds a PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, complemented by demonstrable research or industry experience. Essential qualifications include proven coding skills in software development, particularly in the context of containerized systems, without AI assistance—covering scope, functions, variables, classes, and array methods. You should have a solid understanding of software architecture principles and quality management practices, especially for scalable, modular infrastructures. Experience in handling heterogeneous APIs and integrating HPC scheduler systems such as SLURM is required. Knowledge of quantum computing job characteristics, resource requirements, and familiarity with compiler or transpiler pipelines is highly desirable. Additionally, a good understanding of encryption standards, data protection regulations (especially DSGVO/GDPR), and security protocols is essential. Excellent teamwork, communication skills, and fluency in English (spoken and written) are mandatory to thrive in our collaborative environment. Responsibilities Your primary focus will be implementing a containerized FullStaQD instance as a reference architecture for the project landscape. This involves designing a modular, scalable infrastructure that aligns with best practices in software engineering. You will establish and maintain CI/CD pipelines and automated testing frameworks to ensure high-quality deliverables. Handling heterogeneous APIs and integrating HPC scheduler systems like SLURM into the platform will be critical tasks. Ensuring compliance with data protection and security standards, including DSGVO-compliant encryption, is a fundamental responsibility. Additionally, you will collaborate closely with interdisciplinary teams to develop robust, secure, and efficient solutions that meet the project’s technical and security requirements. Your role will also involve continuous improvement of the platform, documentation, and possibly mentoring junior team members, contributing to the overall success of the GWDG QC ecosystem. Benefits GWDG offers flexible working hours with opportunities for partial remote work, fostering a healthy work-life balance. You will be part of a modern, diverse work environment situated at the crossroads of academia and industry, providing ample opportunities for professional growth and skill development. The position includes social benefits typical of the public sector, such as comprehensive health insurance, pension schemes, and paid leave. Working within a large, internationally recognized IT competence center grants access to cutting-edge technology, collaborative research projects, and a stimulating environment that encourages innovation and continuous learning. Additionally, employees benefit from a supportive organizational culture that values diversity, gender equity, and the inclusion of severely disabled persons, aligning with our commitment to equal opportunity and a respectful workplace. Equal Opportunity The GWDG is committed to promoting diversity and gender equity in the workplace. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive environment. Applications from severely disabled persons are especially encouraged, and we strive to provide equal employment opportunities irrespective of gender, ethnicity, age, or other personal characteristics. Our organization believes that diverse teams drive innovation and excellence, and we are committed to supporting all employees in their professional development.
